questions.question_text: How is the independence of the Internal Audit function established through its reporting lines?
questions.option_a: Reports administratively to the CEO/CFO with no direct Audit Committee reporting
questions.option_b: Reports functionally to the Audit Committee, but plan, budget and CAE appraisal are set by management
questions.option_c: Dual reporting: functionally to the Audit Committee (approves charter, plan and budget), administratively to the CEO
questions.option_d: Audit Committee governs all matters incl. CAE appointment, remuneration and appraisal; independence externally validated

questions.question_text: How are auditor objectivity and freedom from management interference safeguarded?
questions.option_a: Management influences scope, timing or findings; no conflict-of-interest checks
questions.option_b: CAE decides scope, but conflict declarations and staff rotation are informal
questions.option_c: Annual independence declarations, formal rotation policy and unrestricted CAE access to the Audit Committee; interference formally prohibited
questions.option_d: As level C, plus independence and objectivity confirmed by an external quality assessor

questions.question_text: How mature is the whistleblowing and fraud risk process supported by Internal Audit?
questions.option_a: No formal whistleblowing channel or fraud risk assessment
questions.option_b: Basic channel exists but is poorly communicated; fraud considered ad hoc
questions.option_c: Formal, confidential and anonymous channel with Audit Committee oversight; fraud risk built into the audit plan
questions.option_d: Independently reviewed; investigations by certified specialists (e.g., CFE) and fraud analytics in use

questions.question_text: How is the annual audit plan developed and kept current?
questions.option_a: Cyclical schedule without formal risk assessment; plan fixed for the year
questions.option_b: Formal annual risk assessment, but the plan is rarely adjusted in-year
questions.option_c: Risk-based methodology aligned to ERM, strategy and regulatory change; reviewed at least quarterly with Audit Committee approval
questions.option_d: Dynamic plan updated continuously using data analytics and risk indicators; methodology externally benchmarked

questions.question_text: How effectively are emerging risks identified and incorporated into the plan?
questions.option_a: Only when management highlights them
questions.option_b: Discussed informally but not documented
questions.option_c: Systematically identified through horizon scanning and included in the plan
questions.option_d: Advanced tools (AI, external horizon scans) used and independently validated

questions.question_text: How is stakeholder input and assurance coordination built into planning?
questions.option_a: Stakeholder input not formally sought
questions.option_b: Management consulted informally; no structured feedback
questions.option_c: Structured annual consultation with the Board, Audit Committee, management and second-line functions; assurance map maintained
questions.option_d: Continuous engagement through a combined-assurance model; externally benchmarked

questions.question_text: How standardized is the audit methodology and how is professional skepticism applied?
questions.option_a: Methodology varies by auditor; skepticism not emphasized
questions.option_b: Basic methodology applied inconsistently; skepticism covered in training only
questions.option_c: Comprehensive methodology aligned with the IIA Standards, applied consistently; skepticism embedded and reinforced
questions.option_d: Methodology periodically benchmarked and externally validated, including evidence of skepticism

questions.question_text: How is engagement supervision and work paper quality ensured?
questions.option_a: Self-reviewed by the auditor with minimal oversight
questions.option_b: Supervisor review, often incomplete
questions.option_c: Formal supervisory and QA review process documented on every engagement
questions.option_d: Work papers subject to independent QA review as part of external assessment

questions.question_text: How effectively are data analytics and digital audit tools used?
questions.option_a: Manual testing only; no audit management software
questions.option_b: Basic audit management software; analytics used selectively
questions.option_c: Analytics systematically integrated into engagements with automated workflows
questions.option_d: Continuous auditing and monitoring using AI/RPA; independently benchmarked

questions.question_text: How timely, clear and well-communicated are audit reports?
questions.option_a: Often delayed and unclear; communication largely informal
questions.option_b: Issued on time but inconsistent, with limited discussion
questions.option_c: Standardized, timely, risk-rated reports with agreed action plans and formal closing meetings
questions.option_d: Reporting includes KPIs and thematic or trend insights; externally validated

questions.question_text: How are disagreements between management and Internal Audit resolved?
questions.option_a: Escalated informally with no documented process
questions.option_b: Discussed, but management decides
questions.option_c: Formal escalation process; unresolved issues reported to the Audit Committee
questions.option_d: Escalation process independently reviewed

questions.question_text: How are audit issues tracked and management's remediation validated?
questions.option_a: Informal tracking; relies on management's confirmation
questions.option_b: Issues logged; follow-up and validation inconsistent
questions.option_c: Formal system with owners, due dates and status reporting to the Audit Committee; documented verification of remediation
questions.option_d: As level C, plus independent validation of high-priority remediation

questions.question_text: What is the average time to close audit issues?
questions.option_a: Most remain open more than 12 months
questions.option_b: Closed on average within 9–12 months
questions.option_c: Most closed within 6–9 months; overdue items escalated
questions.option_d: Average closure within 3–6 months; independently validated

questions.question_text: How adequate are resources, including use of external specialists?
questions.option_a: Significantly under-resourced; specialists rarely engaged
questions.option_b: Minimum resources; specialists used occasionally
questions.option_c: Resource plan approved by the Audit Committee with a defined co-sourcing and specialist strategy
questions.option_d: Resourcing benchmarked periodically; specialist use strategically planned and evaluated

questions.question_text: How robust is the competency and training program?
questions.option_a: No formal training program
questions.option_b: Limited training not linked to skill gaps
questions.option_c: Formal competency framework with required certifications (CIA, CISA, CFE, SOCPA)
questions.option_d: Competency framework externally benchmarked and validated

questions.question_text: How is IA performance and stakeholder satisfaction measured?
questions.option_a: Not measured
questions.option_b: Measured by audit days or plan completion; informal feedback
questions.option_c: Balanced KPIs (quality, timeliness, value) and annual stakeholder surveys used for improvement
questions.option_d: KPIs and satisfaction benchmarked against peers and externally validated

questions.question_text: How mature is the Quality Assurance and Improvement Program (QAIP)?
questions.option_a: No formal QAIP
questions.option_b: Internal reviews limited in scope
questions.option_c: Comprehensive QAIP with internal assessments and an external assessment at least every 5 years
questions.option_d: More frequent external assessments (e.g., every 3 years) with consistent general conformance

questions.question_text: How does Internal Audit contribute to strategy and adapt to regulatory and technological change?
questions.option_a: Compliance and financial audits only; reacts after changes occur
questions.option_b: Occasional advisory support; changes adopted slowly
questions.option_c: Systematic insight on strategy, risk and governance; plan and methodology adapted proactively
questions.option_d: Trusted strategic advisor with forward-looking insight; adaptability independently assessed

questions.question_text: How effective is Internal Audit in auditing technology and cybersecurity?
questions.option_a: Limited or not conducted
questions.option_b: Basic IT audits lacking depth
questions.option_c: Comprehensive IT audits aligned with NCA ECC, COBIT and ISO 27001
questions.option_d: Independently reviewed; certified specialists perform technology audits

questions.question_text: How effectively does Internal Audit cover regulatory compliance and coordinate with regulators?
questions.option_a: Compliance audits not conducted; minimal regulator interaction
questions.option_b: Limited compliance audits; regulatory updates received passively
questions.option_c: Comprehensive compliance universe (SAMA, CMA, NCA, ZATCA, PDPL) audited; proactive engagement on regulatory findings
questions.option_d: Compliance coverage independently validated and benchmarked; coordination assessed in external QA
